words.sense: sudden seizure of state or institutional power by an elite or military faction
misconceptions: Assuming any political overthrow is a revolution, overlooking that a coup is carried out from the top down by a small insider clique without mass popular mobilization.

words.sense: sweeping transformation of a political or social system driven by mass popular upheaval
misconceptions: Believing revolution simply means any sudden change of government leaders, missing that true revolution requires broad popular participation and deep systemic restructuring.

semantic_axes.description: Small insider elite, military cadre, or executive faction operating from the top down vs. broad popular mobilization spanning diverse social classes from the bottom up.
Replacing individual leaders while leaving legal and administrative machinery intact vs. fundamentally dismantling and remaking the political, social, or constitutional framework.
Swift tactical takeover executed under curfew while ordinary citizens are told to stay indoors vs. mass demonstrations, general strikes, and collective public involvement.

coup: At three in the morning, four tank commanders surrounded the presidential residence, arrested the prime minister in his sleep, and broadcast martial orders over state radio.
The senior officers of the royal guard disarmed the palace sentries, locked the cabinet ministers in the banquet hall, and proclaimed the general as interim ruler.
A faction of five naval captains seized the maritime communication station, grounded civilian airliners, and announced that the civilian parliament was dissolved.
In an overnight operation with zero civilian involvement, the armored division barricaded the supreme court and installed their chief of staff in the executive office.
Two disgruntled colonels led a motorized convoy into the state capital, placed the governor under house arrest, and ordered all civil servants to take orders exclusively from the military council.
The head of the national gendarmerie intercepted the president's motorcade, detained his bodyguards, and seized the executive seal before dawn.
revolution: Millions of citizens across thirty provinces poured into the streets for three weeks, defying police water cannons until the autocratic dynasty collapsed and a democratic constitution was drafted.
General strikes organized by coordinated networks of dockworkers, teachers, and peasant unions paralyzed the country, ultimately abolishing the feudal land system.
Neighborhood assemblies across the nation mobilized millions of families, dismantling the old colonial administration and instituting self-governing municipal communes.
Spurred by soaring grain prices, millions of factory workers and rural laborers converged on the capital, forcing the abdication of the monarch and drafting a republic charter.
Mass civil disobedience spanning student unions, industrial leagues, and civic federations brought the dictatorship to an end, paving the way for complete structural democratization.
From industrial seaports to rural farming cooperatives, the entire populace united in open defiance, tearing down the authoritarian regime and replacing its legal codes.

coup: Tens of thousands of striking miners and their families marched through mountain valleys to the capital, inspiring millions nationwide to demand a constituent assembly.
A grassroots coalition of university students and industrial labor federations mobilized a nationwide general strike that brought down the century-old monarchy.
Across the archipelago, millions of villagers and city dwellers formed local self-governing councils, throwing off royal decrees and establishing a new republic.
Civic associations, market vendors, and dockyard workers united in sustained nationwide rallies, permanently ending military governance and establishing popular rule.
Over three months of continuous public defiance, millions of ordinary people filled the central boulevard every afternoon, demanding systemic constitutional reform.
The entire working populace of the province abandoned their posts, uniting with agrarian leagues to abolish landlord privileges and create cooperative ownership.
revolution: Three disgruntled brigadiers seized the national telecom exchange at midnight and forced the prime minister to sign a transfer of executive powers.
The presidential guard surrounded the legislative palace before dawn, arrested thirty lawmakers, and handed absolute administrative authority to the defense minister.
A small conspiracy of fighter pilots and intelligence officers took control of the airbase, grounded international flights, and declared a military junta.
Without the knowledge of the civilian populace, five army colonels disarmed the interior ministry police and appointed an interim governing council.
The chief of staff used two motorized regiments to cordon off the supreme court and dismiss the elected premier while citizens slept.
An elite military unit detained the regional governor during a private banquet, seizing the provincial broadcasting tower without firing a shot.

edges.boundary_rule: A coup is a swift seizure of institutional control by a small insider or military faction that replaces leadership at the top; a revolution is a broad popular uprising that fundamentally transforms political and social structures.
clues_a: seizure executed by a small cadre of generals, cabinet ministers, or internal plotters
swift capture of administrative buildings, transmission towers, and airports during the night
imposition of strict curfews instructing the civilian population to remain indoors
ouster of top leaders while keeping existing bureaucratic and legal frameworks intact
insider palace or boardroom conspiracy operating without public participation
clues_b: millions of citizens filling public squares across multiple cities and provinces
broad coalition of labor unions, student groups, rural collectives, and civic associations
wholesale abolition of monarchical, dictatorial, or constitutional frameworks
nationwide general strikes paralyzing economic life to force fundamental reform
bottom-up participatory restructuring of political, social, and economic life
irrelevant_clues: whether firearms or military vehicles are visible in the streets
the amount of international news coverage or diplomatic statements
whether the deposed head of state escapes into exile or is placed under house arrest
the geographical size or economic wealth of the nation

misconceptions.M1: Assuming any rapid overthrow of state authority is a revolution, ignoring that an action executed solely by an armed clique or elite cadre is a coup.
misconceptions.M2: Believing a coup must be violent and bloody, overlooking that many coups are quiet, bloodless tactical seizures of executive offices.
misconceptions.M3: Equating revolution with any regime change, failing to recognize that revolution requires mass citizen mobilization and fundamental structural transformation.

chains.frame: The overnight seizure of the maritime authority by three senior port captains was a: ___

beats.text: At midnight, three senior captains of the port police locked the civilian harbor commissioner in his quarters and ordered armed patrol boats to blockade the administrative pier.
beats.decisive_clue: swift armed takeover by three senior port captains locking out the civilian commissioner
beats.reason: The action is an armed, top-down seizure by three insider officers without popular involvement.

beats.text: Before dawn, the captains distributed written notices instructing all civilian crane operators and customs clerks to remain at home until a military port council is seated.
beats.decisive_clue: curfew orders commanding civilian dock personnel to stay home while captains install a council
beats.reason: The captains explicitly exclude the civilian workforce, cementing an insider command takeover.

beats.text: By sunrise, the port captains had confirmed that all existing tariff schedules and maritime statutes would remain unaltered under their emergency stewardship.
beats.decisive_clue: leaving existing tariffs and administrative statutes completely intact
beats.reason: Leaving institutional rules untouched proves this is merely a personnel swap at the executive level.

chains.feedback_short: A swift takeover by a small captain cadre leaving institutional rules untouched is a classic coup.
chains.feedback_deep: The captains use armed force from within the port apparatus to depose their civilian superior. Because ordinary dockworkers are excluded and administrative structures remain identical, the event is an internal power seizure rather than a systemic transformation.
chains.contrast_rule: Small insider seizures replacing top personnel are coups; broad popular uprisings transforming entire systems are revolutions.

hints.attention: Look at who conducted the seizure and whether ordinary workers participated or institutional rules changed.
hints.axis: Small insider elite, military cadre, or executive faction operating from the top down vs. broad popular mobilization spanning diverse social classes from the bottom up.
hints.contrast: Small insider seizures replacing top personnel are coups; broad popular uprisings transforming entire systems are revolutions.

chains.frame: The sudden takeover of the national broadcasting headquarters by the deputy directors was a: ___

beats.text: During the midnight technical maintenance window, two deputy managing directors used private security guards to confiscate the transmission keys from the chief executive.
beats.decisive_clue: deputy directors using private security to seize transmission keys from the chief executive
beats.reason: The ouster is carried out by executive insiders using security staff to seize physical control.

beats.text: The deputy directors immediately cut external studio feeds and broadcast an automated looped message assuring viewers that regular commercial programming would resume under new management.
beats.decisive_clue: automated broadcast promising the resumption of standard commercial programming under new leaders
beats.reason: The plotters promise continuity of existing media programming under their personal control.

beats.text: Network journalists and technical crews arrived in the morning to find the corporate hierarchy unchanged except for the two plotters occupying the penthouse boardroom.
beats.decisive_clue: unchanged corporate hierarchy with plotters simply occupying the executive boardroom
beats.reason: The entire organizational hierarchy persists unaffected, confirming an executive palace replacement.

chains.feedback_short: An internal boardroom takeover replacing the top executive without public mobilization defines a coup.
chains.feedback_deep: The deputy directors execute an insider seizure of studio transmission facilities. No public uprising or systemic reform took place; the existing media corporation continues operating under new executive faces.
chains.contrast_rule: Top-down elite takeovers are coups; mass-led systemic restructuring is a revolution.

hints.attention: Notice whether the broadcast network underwent widespread popular transformation or merely an executive swap.
hints.axis: Small insider elite, military cadre, or executive faction operating from the top down vs. broad popular mobilization spanning diverse social classes from the bottom up.
hints.contrast: Top-down elite takeovers are coups; mass-led systemic restructuring is a revolution.

chains.frame: The midnight march of the armored regiment on the central ministry was a: ___

beats.text: At two in the morning, Colonel Vance led thirty tanks through the quiet avenues of the capital, surrounding the defense ministry and cutting landline cables.
beats.decisive_clue: tank regiment surrounding the defense ministry and cutting communications in the middle of the night
beats.reason: A swift armed operation executed by an army officer targeting executive offices is characteristic of a coup.

beats.decisive_clue: forcing the minister's resignation at weapon point to declare himself commander

chains.contrast_rule: Armed factions seizing palaces under curfew mount coups; mass populations taking over streets create revolutions.

chains.frame: The complete restructuring of the national football federation was a: ___

beats.text: Hundreds of thousands of grassroots supporters, youth coaches, amateur players, and regional club delegates staged coordinated protests across sixty stadiums, demanding an end to decades of aristocratic governance.
beats.decisive_clue: hundreds of thousands of grassroots supporters and amateur delegates staging coordinated protests
beats.reason: The movement is driven by widespread popular participation across thousands of community sports participants.

beats.text: The nationwide coalition ratified an entirely new democratic charter, replacing the lifetime board of governors with elected community councils and redistributing broadcast revenue to local pitches.
beats.decisive_clue: ratifying a new democratic charter and replacing lifetime governors with community councils
beats.reason: Dismantling autocratic governing boards and instituting community democracy transforms the governing system.

beats.text: From remote mountain villages to coastal districts, local sports clubs voted en masse to implement the community constitution, permanently ending oligarchic control over the game.
beats.decisive_clue: widespread nationwide popular implementation of an entirely new community constitution
beats.reason: Mass bottom-up implementation permanently remakes the entire sport's political and financial structure.

chains.feedback_short: A bottom-up transformation led by thousands of grassroots supporters replacing governing structures is a revolution.
chains.feedback_deep: The restructuring of the football league is propelled by massive popular participation across the country. It dismantles old aristocratic privileges and creates an entirely new democratic governance model.
chains.contrast_rule: Broad democratic overhauls are revolutions; small executive conspiracies are coups.

hints.attention: Focus on the scale of participant involvement and whether the structural charter was rewritten.
hints.axis: Small insider elite, military cadre, or executive faction operating from the top down vs. broad popular mobilization spanning diverse social classes from the bottom up.
hints.contrast: Broad democratic overhauls are revolutions; small executive conspiracies are coups.

chains.frame: The sweeping upheaval across the agricultural heartland was a: ___

beats.decisive_clue: two million tenant farmers establishing village committees to abolish feudal landlord ownership

beats.text: The rural committees allied with urban transport unions, forming provincial councils that redistributed arable land to farming families and annulled all peasant debt.
beats.decisive_clue: cross-sector alliance redistributing land and abolishing all peasant debt
beats.reason: Alliances across rural and urban working classes reshaping property and debt laws represent deep systemic transformation.

beats.text: Within six months, the old feudal legal code was formally burned in town squares, replaced by a cooperatively governed agrarian commonwealth.
beats.decisive_clue: burning the feudal legal code and creating a cooperatively governed agrarian commonwealth
beats.reason: The total destruction of the old legal foundation and establishment of a new social order cements the revolution.

chains.feedback_short: Mass mobilization across millions of rural workers abolishing feudalism and establishing cooperative governance constitutes a revolution.
chains.feedback_deep: The agricultural transformation involves millions of working people acting collectively to overturn centuries-old socio-economic hierarchies. It completely replaces the legal and property system.
chains.contrast_rule: Mass collective transformation of society is a revolution; narrow palace takeovers are coups.

chains.frame: The sudden toppling of the colonial regime across the archipelago was a: ___

beats.decisive_clue: four senior naval officers detaining the governor and proclaiming martial rule

beats.text: Declassified dispatches revealed the officers acted under orders from a clandestine island-wide network: within hours, three hundred thousand islanders surrounded the garrison, disarmed sentries, and burned the colonial charter.
beats.decisive_clue: officers executing directives from an island-wide movement of three hundred thousand citizens abolishing the colonial charter
beats.reason: Revealing the officers were merely an armed vanguard directed by three hundred thousand mobilizing citizens flips the event into a revolution.

beats.text: Island elders, student syndicates, and harbor workers established a constituent assembly that wrote the archipelago's first independent democratic constitution.
beats.decisive_clue: popular constituent assembly drafting the archipelago's first independent constitution
beats.reason: Broad participatory assembly writing an independent democratic constitution confirms a lasting popular revolution.

chains.feedback_short: Evidence that the officers acted for a mass movement of three hundred thousand islanders flips the takeover to a revolution.
chains.feedback_deep: What initially appeared to be an isolated military coup by four naval officers was actually the coordinated opening phase of a popular uprising. Because hundreds of thousands of islanders mobilized to abolish colonial institutions and establish a democratic constitution, the event was a revolution.
chains.contrast_rule: A military strike directed by mass popular mobilization to abolish an entire system is a revolution.

hints.attention: Notice who truly directed the naval officers and whether the broader populace mobilized to replace the system.

beats.text: The entire extended family established an egalitarian trust where women and younger cousins hold equal voting power and revenue rights.
beats.decisive_clue: establishing an egalitarian trust with equal voting rights for women and younger relatives
beats.reason: Establishing equal voting and revenue rights for all household members confirms the structural revolution.

Because the entire multigenerational family mobilized to dismantle patriarchal succession and establish an egalitarian trust, the restructuring was a revolution.

chains.frame: The sudden fall of the provincial government was a: ___

beats.text: Following weeks of general strikes, hundreds of thousands of citizens stormed the provincial palace, disarmed the guards, and forced the autocratic governor to sign an immediate surrender of executive power.
beats.decisive_clue: hundreds of thousands of citizens storming the palace and forcing the governor's surrender
beats.reason: The government falls through a direct mass popular storming of the executive palace.

beats.text: However, intelligence logs reveal the palace guards were ordered to yield by four dissident generals who had already arrested the governor hours earlier in his bunker, orchestrating the surrender to install their own military junta before the crowd arrived.
beats.decisive_clue: intelligence logs revealing four generals had already arrested the governor in his bunker to install a junta
beats.reason: Evidence that the actual power seizure was executed in secret by four generals flips the fall of government to a coup.

beats.text: The generals immediately turned the palace cannons on the crowd, declared martial law, and announced that all provincial statutes and elite property rights remained strictly preserved.
beats.decisive_clue: turning cannons on the crowd and preserving all existing statutes and property rights
beats.reason: Violent suppression of the public and total preservation of existing statutes confirm an elite military coup.

chains.feedback_short: Secret logs showing four generals detained the governor beforehand to install a junta flip the event to a coup.
chains.feedback_deep: Although the palace appeared to fall to hundreds of thousands of storming citizens, the decisive seizure of executive power was accomplished hours earlier by four military insiders. Because the true transfer of authority was an armed top-down conspiracy that suppressed the populace and preserved elite laws, it was a coup.
chains.contrast_rule: A secret military seizure of executive power is a coup, even when masked by popular unrest.

hints.attention: Look at who actually detained the governor and whether state power was seized by generals or the crowd.
hints.axis: Small insider elite, military cadre, or executive faction operating from the top down vs. broad popular mobilization spanning diverse social classes from the bottom up.
hints.contrast: A secret military seizure of executive power is a coup, even when masked by popular unrest.

beats.reason: Two individuals unilaterally seizing household assets and imposing rules on housemates constitutes an insider coup.

beats.text: However, a shared group journal revealed the two acted as designated executors of a unanimous pact made by all seven housemates to abolish room seniority and institute equal consensus governance.

beats.reason: Reframing the action as the collective mandate of all seven housemates abolishing hierarchy reframes it as an egalitarian revolution.

beats.text: The shared house established an open communal ledger where rent was split proportionally to income and no individual member held governing seniority.
beats.decisive_clue: open communal ledger splitting rent by income and eliminating governing seniority
beats.reason: Proportional income splitting and elimination of seniority establish a permanent structural revolution in the home.

chains.feedback_deep: The scenario initially appeared to be an authoritarian insider power grab by two roommates. chains.contrast_rule: Moving from an exclusive power grab to an inclusive structural democracy reframes a coup into a revolution.
